_comment: Skill Repo Spec v1 s9 -- every path in this repo belongs to exactly one class.
TOOL    = code, SKILL.md, docs, reference data, and metrics ABOUT THE SKILL. Public.
FIXTURE = LIFELIKE test data: rows that look like real records, whose real version is
sitting right there in the operator's life and is structurally indistinguishable.
Must be produced by tools/make_fixtures.py -- a real record cannot be regenerated,
so pasting one in fails at commit. (A self-evidently fake canary or an Acme mock is
NOT lifelike and does not need a generator; the risk it guards against is a person
reaching for a convenient REAL example, and there is no temptation to reach for a
real value that would look obviously wrong next to FAKE_CANARY_XYZ.)
DATA    = anything a REAL RUN produced. Never git-tracked. Lives in the private companion
config, resolved at runtime by tools/datadir.py. This repo ships only the schema.
data_sealed = a path that HELD real data, was purged, and must stay dead.
Enforced by tools/data_boundary.py in .githooks and in CI.
_audited: 2026-07-31 RE-AUDIT (supersedes the 2026-07-13 sweep, which recorded an empty declaration for this repo). The earlier sweep asked only whether shipped code appends to a TRACKED file here. That question is too narrow: it clears every path that is gitignored, and .gitignore is advisory -- `git add -f` walks straight through it, which is the whole reason declarations exist. This pass asked instead whether shipped code or shipped docs can put REAL-RUN OUTPUT at a repo-relative path at all. ANSWER: YES, and it is among the most sensitive output in the fleet: a screenshot plus a full accessibility-tree dump of whatever was on the operator's actual screen. capture.py defaults out_dir to the OS temp dir, which is outside any repo, but --out-dir is a plain flag and `--out-dir .` run from here drops screen.png, annotated.png and elements.json into the repo root under exactly those names. This repo's .gitignore already lists all three. They are declared data_sealed rather than data on purpose: two of the three are PNG bitmaps, for which a .example is not a schema but a decoy file, and the third travels with them as one capture. data_sealed is checked identically to data (never tracked) and owes no schema, which is the honest mechanical fit. No directory-form declaration is possible here because the run directory name is a timestamp and this checker matches by prefix, not by glob.
_data_home: ~/.screen-vision-config/data/   (override with $SCREEN_VISION_DATA_DIR). If this skill ever needs to record real-run output, it goes THERE -- never back into this repo.
